steps.title: Deterministic build and pinned toolchain
steps.what: Zero-dependency build script; Node pinned (.nvmrc, engines); LF and BOM normalization; file-type allowlist; stored zip with fixed timestamps and order
steps.done: Two builds on different machines produce identical SHA256SUMS and an identical zip
steps.needs: Add me to the GitHub repo, or I create it and transfer ownership to you

steps.title: Hash list and reproducibility check in CI
steps.what: sha256sum-compatible hash list; PR workflow builds twice in separate folders and compares; hash list uploaded as an artifact
steps.done: A PR fails if the two builds differ by a single byte

steps.title: Three trust tiers with short-lived tokens
steps.what: PR jobs get no id-token at all; staging and release environments; required reviewer on release; OIDC sub claim customized to repo + environment + workflow file; actions pinned to commit SHAs
steps.done: A PR job cannot obtain any cloud token; a staging token cannot assume the release role
steps.deliverable: Workflow permissions, environment settings, sub-claim config
steps.needs: Approve the environment and reviewer settings I send (10 minutes)

steps.title: Signed-tag release gate
steps.what: Annotated SSH-signed tag whose message is the hash list; allowed signers read from the protected release environment; tag must equal manifest version; clean rebuild compared file for file
steps.done: Unsigned tag, unknown key, late code change or wrong version each stop the release (automated tests)
steps.needs: Send the public SSH key(s) of whoever signs releases

steps.title: MV3 shell with minimum permissions
steps.what: Manifest with activeTab and scripting only; one host permission (your backend); CSP connect-src locked to the backend; module service worker; popup; on-demand injection, no static content scripts
steps.done: chrome.storage does not exist at runtime; a fetch to any other origin is blocked by CSP (browser test)

steps.title: Ticket handoff and backend fetch
steps.what: Web app sends a short-lived ticket via externally_connectable; sender origin checked; ticket kept in memory only; active tab must match the ticket's portal; fetch with no-store, no credentials, no redirects; response shape validated
steps.done: Wrong site, expired ticket and messages from other sites are refused, and nothing is filled
steps.needs: Ticket and fill-values API contract (from the AWS engineer)

steps.title: Field discovery on third-party pages
steps.what: Signals from labels, aria-labelledby, aria-label, placeholder, title, name/id, autocomplete; open shadow roots; visibility; fillable field kinds; embedded frames counted and reported
steps.done: Every field in the sample portals, including shadow DOM, is discovered with the right signals
steps.needs: List of target portals, plus test pages or test accounts

steps.title: Exact-one-match-or-skip matcher
steps.what: Candidate set per value; two-way uniqueness (one value, one field); explicit skip reasons; matching rules frozen and shipped inside the signed extension
steps.done: Ambiguous, shared-field and no-match cases fill nothing (unit tests)

steps.title: Value safety checks
steps.what: maxlength, pattern, input type, single matching select option, date format only when the field states it, never overwrite, read-only and disabled, passwords and files excluded, backend value format
steps.done: Each rule has a passing unit test that proves the skip

steps.title: Fill writer and review highlights
steps.what: Native value setters plus input and change events (works with React and Angular forms); read-back; filled fields outlined solid, ambiguous ones dashed; clear highlights; never submits or clicks
steps.done: Values survive the page re-rendering; the submit counter stays at zero (browser test)

steps.title: Weekly checkpoint 1 (written)
steps.what: What's done, what's next, decisions needed, explicit actions for you
steps.done: Sent Friday Oct 9
steps.needs: Read and answer any decisions listed

steps.title: Zero-storage and zero-logging enforcement
steps.what: Policy gate in CI (storage, logging, submission, dynamic code, network egress, permissions, CSP); worker strips reports to statuses and reasons; errors as codes, never messages with data
steps.done: The gate fails on each injected violation (tests) and passes on the release build

steps.title: Unit test suite
steps.what: Matcher fixtures from real portal patterns; hash list; build determinism incl. Windows line endings; zip and CRX parsing; policy gate
steps.done: All green in CI on every PR

steps.title: Real-browser tests
steps.what: Playwright on real Chromium with the exact release files; extension loaded unpacked; full ticket to fill chain against a local HTTPS mirror of the backend origin
steps.done: All green in CI; values never appear in the popup report

steps.title: Staging pipeline and Web Store upload
steps.what: GitHub OIDC to Google Workload Identity Federation to a service account; Chrome Web Store API v2 upload to the staging item; first submission early to start the review clock
steps.done: Staging upload runs from CI with no stored secret
steps.needs: Chrome Web Store developer account and item; Google Cloud project (I send the exact commands)

steps.title: Published-package verifier
steps.what: Downloads the CRX the store serves; parses CRX3; hashes every file; compares with the signed list; store additions handled by an explicit, printed allowlist
steps.done: Passes on the store's package; fails on any other difference (tests)

steps.title: Install procedure and runbooks
steps.what: Install: Web Store listing, managed install by policy, unpacked for testing; release runbook; your-side checklist
steps.done: Someone other than me can cut a release from the runbook

steps.title: End-to-end release dry run
steps.what: Sign tag, run the gate, upload to staging, verify the package
steps.done: One full release completes from a signed tag with no manual edits

steps.title: Acceptance run against your written criteria
steps.what: Walk all 16 steps' acceptance criteria and fix anything that falls short
steps.done: Every criterion marked pass with evidence

steps.title: Working build handover and checkpoint 2
steps.what: Recorded walkthrough, written update, what remains for Nov 1
steps.done: Working build delivered Thursday Oct 15

buffer.title: Acceptance window until the hard deadline
buffer.what: Your review, Web Store review turnaround, fixes from acceptance. Included in the fixed price.

actions.action: Add me to the GitHub repository (or approve my transfer of a new one)
actions.why: CI, environments and branch rules live there

actions.action: Approve the staging and release environment settings I send, and name the release reviewer
actions.why: Release jobs wait for this reviewer

actions.action: Send the public SSH key of each person allowed to sign releases
actions.why: The release gate only trusts these keys

actions.action: Share the ticket and fill-values API contract (from the AWS engineer)
actions.why: The extension's only network call depends on it

actions.action: List the target portals, with test pages or test accounts if they exist
actions.why: Matching rules are tuned against real forms

actions.action: Read checkpoint 1 and answer any decisions in it
Create or confirm the Chrome Web Store developer account and staging item
actions.why: Needed before the first upload (one-time US$5 fee)

actions.action: Create a Google Cloud project, or let me run the setup commands I send
actions.why: Workload Identity Federation for keyless publishing

actions.action: Review the working build and the acceptance checklist

assumptions.assumption: The 16 written steps match this breakdown in scope
assumptions.otherwise: Re-estimate within a day of reading them

assumptions.assumption: The ticket and fill-values API exists or is stubbed by Oct 7
assumptions.otherwise: I write the contract and a stub with the AWS engineer

assumptions.assumption: Up to about 10 target portals with ordinary HTML forms
assumptions.otherwise: Each heavily scripted or multi-step portal needs its own fixtures and rules

assumptions.assumption: Fields are in the top page or open shadow roots, not cross-origin frames
assumptions.otherwise: Frame support means per-frame injection and matching

assumptions.assumption: Matching rules ship inside the extension (signed with each release)
assumptions.otherwise: If rules come from the backend per portal, they need their own signing and review path

assumptions.assumption: Chrome only (Edge works from the same package)
assumptions.otherwise: Firefox needs a second manifest and build target

assumptions.assumption: 'Stores nothing' allows the in-memory ticket in the service worker
assumptions.otherwise: If even that is out, the web app must hand over the ticket at fill time
